standard_prerequisites: the categories C of inverse systems (B_n) of discrete A/I^n-modules with the compatibility conditions and C' of I-adically complete A-algebras, with the functors between them (equations of the same section)
the limit lemma: B = lim B_n is I-adically complete with B/I^nB = B_n (Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-limit-complete)
completeness of the completed polynomial ring A[x_1,...,x_r]^wedge = lim A_n[x_1,...,x_r]
the surjectivity criterion for maps into complete rings: a map surjective modulo I into a complete target is surjective (Algebra, Lemma algebra-lemma-completion-generalities)
core_obligations: Prove that the functor (B_n) -> B = lim B_n is a quasi-inverse to the functor from C' to C, and that the completions A[x_1,...,x_r]^wedge lie in C' with every object of C' of the form A[x_1,...,x_r]^wedge / J
proof_roadmap: For (B_n) in C, the limit lemma gives B I-adically complete with B/I^nB = B_n, so B is in C' and taking quotients recovers the system, and conversely every B in C' satisfies B = lim B/I^nB.
The completed polynomial ring is a limit of the A_n[x_1,...,x_r], hence an object of C' by the first part.

For B in C', choose b_1,...,b_r generating B/IB over A/I; completeness extends the map A[x_1,...,x_r] -> B to A[x_1,...,x_r]^wedge -> B, and the surjectivity criterion makes this map surjective, exhibiting B as a quotient.
difficulty_reason: H2: a completeness bookkeeping lemma with two short applications of standard completion lemmas.
